sources.entry: vegvisir - Browser based GUI for LLDB Debugger.

summary.one_liner: Vegvisir is a browser-based graphical front end for the LLDB debugger, run as a local Python web app.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a browser-based GUI for the LLDB debugger, started by running vegvisir.py and then pointing a browser at the local server. Its listed views are index, auto_suggest, target_create, disassembly, funcs_imported, sections, strings, and help, which suggests it handles loading a target, disassembling code, listing imported functions and sections, and browsing strings. It uses Capstone, and the README's TODO list mentions a planned hex memory view with search and command auto-suggest. The author describes the code as rough and unreliable in places, and the README has no screenshot content.
use_cases: debug programs with LLDB from a web browser
list imported functions and sections of a target
use a GUI instead of the LLDB command line
how_to_run: Open the browser at the address the server prints
notable: Browser-based frontend for LLDB, no native GUI toolkit
Views for disassembly, imported functions, sections, and strings
Planned hex memory view with search and lisa.py support
caveats: Requires the system Python at /usr/bin/python, which the README says LLDB on macOS supports; written for Python 2.7
The author says the code is poor quality and the LLDB controller is not reliable yet
Several features (hex view, pip packaging, keyboard shortcuts) are still TODO
